title: Khronos SimpleTexture at exactly four texels per pixel -- the corpus's only case where minification decides every covered pixel

criterion.says: A simple glTF asset with a texture.

acceptanceClass.because: The sibling case's construction at four times the distance: a unit square in the plane z = 0 seen along its own normal with no roll, so its four edges are at slopes 0/1 and 1/0 and |n| = 1, and the scale and aim put every constant at half a lattice step -- a margin of 0.5 px, the largest the family admits and 100 times the oracle's own 0.005 px filter half-width. The distance changes what the SAMPLER does and not what the SILHOUETTE does.

subjects.name: SimpleTexture
subjects.notes: A unit quad in the XY plane at z = 0, front face towards +Z, with TEXCOORD_0 putting the image upright when the quad is seen from +Z with +Y up: the vertex at (0,0,0) carries uv (0,1) and the one at (0,1,0) carries uv (0,0), which is glTF's origin at the image's UPPER left. No NORMAL, and none is needed: a Lambertian facet under a uniform environment returns rho*L whichever way it faces.

source.pinReason: the same pin every other Khronos subject in this tree carries

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

camera.derivation: EXACTLY FOUR TEXELS PER PIXEL, WHICH IS WHAT PUTS MINIFICATION IN THE COMPARISON. It is this case's whole reason to exist: measured on the corpus as it stood, `simple-texture` read NO mip level above 0 at any pixel and `normal-tangent` read one at about 920 of 921 600, so a filter correction had nothing to be judged on (board:1130). Same lens as the sibling case -- yfov = 2*atan((24/2)/50), so tan(yfov/2) = 0.24 exactly -- giving 720/(0.48*d) px per metre at the subject's plane. The image is 256 texels across the quad's 1 m, so texels per pixel is 256*0.48*d/720 = d/5.859375, and d = 23.4375 m gives 4 EXACTLY. The quad is then 64 px on a side and lambda = log2(4) = 2, so every covered pixel reads mip level 2 and none reads level 0. THE EDGES STILL LAND ON PIXEL BOUNDARIES: the optical axis maps to raster (639.5, 359.5) and the half-extent is 32 px, so the silhouette runs 607.5..671.5 and 327.5..391.5 -- every edge half a lattice step from every pixel centre, the same 0.5 px best case the sibling holds. AND LEVEL 2 IS READ AT ONE TEXEL PER PIXEL: level 2 of a 256 texel chain is 64 texels across the same 1 m, so the covered pixel 0.5 px inside the left edge sits at u = 0.5/64, texel 0's centre exactly. The filter is therefore taken back OUT within the level, and what remains in the comparison is the only question this case is for -- whether our level 2 carries what Cycles integrates over the same four texels. The roll is zero for the sibling's reason.
camera.note: The glTF carries no camera; this case declares its own and the oracle builds the same one from these numbers. Only the distance differs from `render/texture/simple-texture`.

light.note: The only illumination is Blender's factory world. A uniform environment is what makes a Lambertian facet return rho*L with no integration left, and rho here is the file's own texel.

world.note: Configured by not being configured. The observed colour and strength go into provenance.json, so a Blender that changed them is visible without any machinery that refuses.

material.note: THE ORACLE IS LOWERED, NOT THE TOLERANCE (board:0087). The importer builds a Principled BSDF whose specular lobe survives metallicFactor 0 at IOR 1.5, so a render through it has an integral left and no closed form to be judged against. This arm keeps exactly what the asset is for -- its own base-colour image, its uv set and its sampler -- and rewires that image into a Diffuse BSDF at roughness 0, whose Cycles closure is max(dot(N,w),0)/pi. Under the factory world that is rho(u,v)*L per texel. The image datablock is untouched, so its sRGB decode still happens at the texel and before the interpolation, which is the convention TextureLinearInterpolationTest decides and the one our sRGB texture VIEW puts in the sampler. THE CLOSURE IS DECLARED: this subject is a single unoccluded facet, the one shape where the diffuse arm's closed form rho*L survives, so it takes that arm rather than the emitter a self-shading subject needs.

default.note: THE ONE RECIPE IN THIS TREE THAT INTEGRATES A PIXEL, and the case is useless without it. Every other case renders one sample through a 0.01 px box, which -- as those manifests say -- makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does. That recipe CANNOT ADJUDICATE A TEXTURE FILTER: it point-samples, so any filtering the engine does is a departure from it. Measured on this case, both directions: our single-level render is 0.190 codes from the 1-sample oracle and 37.864 from this one; our mip-filtered render is 37.412 from the 1-sample oracle and 5.340 from this one, INSIDE the picture bound. The oracle also disagrees with ITSELF by up to 37.880 codes between the two recipes, over 267 of 12 288 channels. 256 samples over a full-pixel box is the integral the rasteriser's mip chain approximates; a diffuse-only scene at zero bounces under a uniform world has no light-transport noise left, so the only thing the samples vary is the position within the pixel, which is exactly the quantity being integrated.

notes: The sibling `render/texture/simple-texture` states this asset at one texel per pixel so no filter is integrating anything. This case states the same asset at four, so a filter is integrating everything -- the corpus had no such case, and without one a mip chain, an index rule and a Toksvig term were all being judged at pixels they do not reach.

subjectFrameFraction.derivation: the quad is a plane perpendicular to the optical axis, so its perspective image is a similarity: 1 m at 64 px per metre is 64 px on a side, and 64*64/(1280*720) = 4096/921600. Recomputed by the runner from the fetched vertices and refused on a mismatch.
subjectFrameFraction.note: What the boundary bound is applied UNDER: a camera that framed the subject smaller would tighten the bound without saying so.

reductions.because: Under minification the two sides FILTER, and they filter with different implementations: this engine samples a mip chain on the device and Cycles filters through its own texture system. Bit-equality between two filter implementations is not a property either can offer, and this case exists precisely to put four texels under one pixel. [MEASURED] 8569 of 12288 channels differ where the 1:1 sibling differs by at most 5 ulps -- so the divergence is the FILTER and not the decode, and the sibling is what says so. The case's own subject is decided by `picture_p99_delta_code`, which passes at 0 codes against a bound of 6.4354338.
